newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir warns against backing U.S. non-trade move.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir warns against backing U.S. non-trade move.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday warned the country's activist groups and trade unions against supporting U.S. efforts to include non-trade issues in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting.
If non-trade issues were included in the meeting, Malaysian workers would be the losers, the national Bernama news agency quoted Mahathir as telling reporters.
The WTO ministerial meeting is being held in Singapore this week.

The real reason Washington was pushing for the inclusion of non-trade issues was not because it was concerned about labour standards but because it wants to undermine Malaysia's competitiveness, Mahathir said.
"If we support them, one day we will end up being unemployed while the ones who are working will be those from developed countries," he said.

The United States is pushing for international trade rules to raise developing country labour standards, eradicate sweat shops and stop an estimated 250 million children working. It wants the WTO ministerial meeting to move on the issue.
But many developing countries say the proposal is a protectionist ploy, and argue that both their economies and their workers would be worse off with such rules.
